newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire army plans air strikes against rebels.
newsitem.headline: Zaire army plans air strikes against rebels.

text.p: Zaire's army now plans to use aircraft and helicopter gunships against rebels in the east after rebel thrusts on several fronts blunted its much-touted counter-offensive.

The rebels, for their part, claimed fresh advances on the battlefield and said they would now target Kisangani, Zaire's third largest city and headquarters for the counter-offensive launched by the army on January 20.
Zaire's main opposition grouping, whose leader backs negotiations to end the conflict, called a general strike for Monday as part of its campaign to bring down Prime Minister Leon Kengo wa Dondo.

"The army will rely heavily on air strikes to defeat the rebels," a Defence Ministry official told Reuters. "The counter-offensive has been launched but it has not got into high gear. We are getting ready for a very decisive action."
Helicopter gunships and attack aircraft have been seen at Kisangani airport for several weeks.

Rebel leader Laurent Kabila said at his Goma headquarters that Zaire's mercenary-backed army used Mi-24 Russian helicopter gunships on Friday to attack rebel positions near the town of Lubutu, about 200 km (125 miles) from Kisangani, but failed to dislodge his forces.
The Defence Ministry official said the main problem was refuelling and pinpointing rebel positions on a very fluid front.
"We have enough fighter planes to fight the war to the end but we have to gather as much information as possible on the rebel positions. That's why things seem to be taking time," he said.
The rebel advances in the east further endangered up to 300,000 trapped Hutu refugees who fled Rwanda fearing reprisals after the 1994 genocide of minority Tutsis by hardline Hutus.
Approaching 130,000 refugees are camped around the village of Tingi Tingi, close to Lubutu, and up to 30 a day are reported dying from hunger or disease.

A further 40,000 exhausted Hutus have set up camp five km (three miles) to the southeast after walking 70 km (45 miles) from Amisi where rebels took control of the landing strip and refugee camp on Friday.

With the army and rebels swapping claims and counter-claims over which towns they control, refugees have voted with their feet while witnesses said Zairean civilians had abandoned their villages around Tingi Tingi and Lubutu.
Kabila said he had ordered his forces not to advance on Tingi Tingi, which U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees Sadako Ogata visited on Saturday.
She expressed concern about the threat to the trapped refugees and said the only solution was for the refugees to return home to Rwanda.

Kabila said his forces were consolidating around Kindu airbase, on the Zaire River over 400 km (250 miles) upstream from Kisangani, and closing in on the Lake Tanganyika port of Moba in the mineral-rich southern province of Shaba.
